article_title: Fostering innovation, inclusion, and diversity in astronomy education: The Czech Astronomy Olympiad experience
citation: Pavlík, V., Vošmera, J., Gráf, T., & Křížová, R. (2024). Fostering Innovation, Inclusion, and Diversity in Astronomy Education: The Czech Astronomy Olympiad Experience. https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.12376
title: Czech Astronomy Olympiad: a multi-round, multi-age-category national astronomy competition
description: The Czech Astronomy Olympiad (CzAO) is an extra-curricular competition for secondary-school and high-school students, founded in 2003 and organised by the Czech Astronomical Society. It uses "four age categories: AB (for the oldest students), CD, EF, and GH (for the youngest ones)", merging pairs of consecutive school grades because astronomy is not part of the standard Czech school curriculum. Each academic year proceeds through a supervised in-person school round with multiple-choice and computational problems, a take-home regional round including an observational exercise, and a countrywide final in Prague or Opava that includes data-analysis questions, night-sky observations, and planetarium orientation tasks.
requirements: Organisation by the Czech Astronomical Society with annual announcement among top-tier competitions by the Czech Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports
Teachers supervising the school round and a Board of CzAO grading the regional round
constraints: Astronomy is not part of the standard school curriculum in the Czech Republic, which the article says makes assigning topics to individual school grades challenging
target_learners: secondary-school and high-school students in the Czech Republic
examples: Approximately 25 top-ranked students from each category are selected for the countrywide final round, and all students may attempt any higher-grade category

title: CzAO online platform: computer-based school round, online regional round, and remote submission and grading modules
description: CzAO uses online platforms to inform students and teachers about the competition and has progressively digitised its rounds. "Since 2010, we have enabled the students to solve the school round on a computer", and a later module let students solve regional-round multiple-choice questions and enter the observational part online. During the Covid-19 lockdown the organisers "added another module for submitting scanned documents to our websites and enabled each student to upload their work online", allowing the Board to evaluate scans remotely from the Czech Republic, Germany, Switzerland and the USA. The article states these initiatives eased administration and evaluation and helped engage students from diverse geographical locations.
requirements: A dedicated website environment (https://olympiada.astro.cz/) with modules for online solving, document upload, and remote grading
constraints: The government suspended funding for all student competitions and schools were closed during the Covid-19 lockdown, which the online system helped the competition survive
target_learning_goals: access to astronomy competition participation regardless of physical location
examples: Teachers previously downloaded, printed and distributed school-round exercises and mailed regional-round solutions to the Board before the online transition

title: Open Access English-language booklets of CzAO competition problems with solved problems
description: CzAO publishes its competition problems, translated from Czech into English, in open-access booklets (published for 2015/16 through 2022/23, with DOIs on Zenodo). The article states that "several years ago, we also started to translate our competition problems into English and publish them in open-access booklets", that the initiative "was met with positive feedback from our international colleagues", and that some foreign Olympiads use them to prepare their students for competition rounds. The booklets are edited by the CzAO team and released with solved problems to make astronomical knowledge accessible to a global audience.
requirements: Translation of competition problems into English
Publication under open access (Zenodo DOIs printed in the article's reference list)
target_learners: international astronomy olympiad students and educators
examples: Some foreign Olympiads use the booklets to prepare their students for their competition rounds
